title: Eliminate protected media URL leakage and repeated 401 thumb noise

title: Reduce Vault startup session latency and critical-request chaining
summary: Shorten the initial /vault startup chain by reducing duplicate session work, improving session endpoint latency, and trimming avoidable render-blocking and startup-layout cost without destabilizing beta debugging.
notes: Opened on 2026-04-14 from live DevTools traces during Vault crash and recovery work. The page is currently usable, but startup still pays heavily for api/auth/session, duplicate auth/session resolution, and some first-render layout work. Moved to In Progress on 2026-04-14 after the auth bootstrap was tightened to wait for Firebase token resolution before loading /api/auth/session, a low-risk preconnect hint was added for identitytoolkit.googleapis.com, the first catalog fetch was switched to reuse the already-resolved auth token, the Vault catalog load effect was narrowed to real browse-access signals instead of the whole session object, protected auth-control mutations were switched to reuse the resolved token, stale startup session/catalog requests were made abortable, the server-side metadata access token used by the session path was cached in-process until near expiry, and session timing instrumentation was added for future authenticated trace analysis. A fresh unauthenticated browser trace now shows a single /api/auth/session request on startup. Quick public-route verification did not surface the new timing headers or opt-in debug payload yet, so the next pass should verify how those values behave through the full hosting path before relying on them. Remaining work should verify the authenticated trace path and then profile the next safe startup/layout reductions.

title: Define downloader packaging and export options
summary: Ship the first local-catalog export flow with manifest CSV packaging, asset bundling, and automatic multi-zip sharding for larger catalogs.
notes: Moved to In Progress on 2026-04-15. A first working Tier 1 local export path now exists in suno-viewer: authenticated users with `catalog.export.local` can prepare a local catalog package, download a manifest CSV, and fetch one or more ZIP parts built from workspace-scoped audio, lyrics, and image assets. Sharding now targets a practical max part size instead of one giant archive so larger catalogs can split cleanly across multiple downloads. The 2026-04-18 through 2026-04-23 UX passes added an active queue/readiness model via `/api/catalog-exports`, simple ready-download rows with type/size/download actions, phase+step messaging for active packages, ready-state notifications, a first-class Downloads shell destination, short song-key-based asset filenames, unique per-part manifest names to avoid Windows unzip/copy conflicts, cleaner empty/error handling for non-exportable workspaces, calmer failure copy with direct support actions, removal of fake zero-byte success metrics, and removal of the one-option workspace picker in the single-workspace case. On 2026-05-16 the long-running export durability pass finally closed the full-catalog blocker: full export now completes `ready` on the new domains with authenticated manifest and ZIP-part downloads verified, using a stabilized 1.0 GB sharding profile plus server-side cleanup of uploaded temporary ZIPs. On 2026-05-17 a fresh selected-songs package (`9a1907147a667431`) was created and verified live through ready state on `sundrop.music`, and the restored history listing was also rechecked with both that new selection export and the existing full-catalog export (`6da643bd895b8b8d`) returning healthy manifest, summary, and ZIP URLs. Remaining work should focus on turning Downloads into a more persistent customer history center and refining broader packaging UX rather than basic export survival.

On 2026-04-12 the Vault shell split the search row from the control row and added the first catalog-mode controls, so this ticket now owns tightening those controls into a clearer structured retrieval band. First live slice shipped on 2026-05-17: lyrics-state and publish-state dropdowns are now live in production, and active chips now surface query, account, removed, lyrics, and publish narrowing with one-click clear. A second live narrowing slice shipped on 2026-06-15 on revision `suno-viewer-00184-ghq`: the retrieval band now includes a dedicated `Filter style or tag` field that narrows against `displayTags`, `tags`, `styles`, and `styleText` without consuming the main search box. title: Improve Vault search relevance and match visibility
summary: Improve search ranking, exact-match prioritization, and matched-field visibility so users understand why results appear.
notes: Later-phase search quality work should weight title matches over tags/styles/lyrics, support more intuitive ranking, and make the match reason visible in the result cards where practical. Moved to In Progress on 2026-05-17 after the first visible relevance pass shipped to production: search results now surface `Matched on ...` context inside both Vault Grid cards and Music Catalog rows, including lyric excerpts when the query lands in lyrics text. Reconfirmed live on revision `suno-viewer-00179-vpv` after the production bundle mismatch was resolved. The first ranking pass then shipped on revision `suno-viewer-00180-ctx`: query-active retrieval now sorts by field-aware relevance first so exact title and account hits outrank broader style/tag/lyrics matches, with the manual sort acting as the tiebreaker. A second tuning pass shipped on 2026-06-15 on revision `suno-viewer-00189-mv2`: search now normalizes punctuation-heavy titles more gracefully, supports multi-token matching across fields such as account plus lyrics, and rejects misleading partial multi-token hits that only satisfy part of the user intent. Remaining work is live tuning against ambiguous catalog queries and deciding whether any explicit relevance controls should surface in the UI.

title: Track edge cases and production anomalies
summary: Create a real home for malformed data, runtime oddities, import anomalies, and product edge cases that are too important to lose but too cross-cutting to force into a single lane.
notes: Opened on 2026-04-10. This epic owns weird-but-real production behavior such as malformed Vault imports, stale media fallbacks, partial enrichments, and customer-visible anomalies that need tracking even when they span harvest, Vault UI, auth, and media handling.

title: Define minimum viable song thresholds across import, Vault, and publish
summary: Define how incomplete a song record can be before harvest should reject it, Vault should hide it, or publish should block it, and then apply those rules consistently.
notes: Opened on 2026-04-10 from the malformed gravitystruth Vault row. This ticket is not about one song only; it owns the minimum viable song rule set. It should answer which fields are required for import acceptance, which are required for Vault display, which are required for playback, and which are required before a song can be queued or published.

title: Serve private song media without stale public fallback behavior
summary: Define and implement the correct behavior when artwork or audio exists only as private gs:// media so the Vault uses guarded app delivery instead of stale or incorrect public CDN guesses.
notes: Opened on 2026-04-10 from the gravitystruth artwork and audio mismatch. This ticket covers private-media proxying, fallback order, and when the Vault should show media-unavailable versus silently displaying the wrong artwork or audio.

title: Keep published Vault catalog freshness aligned with live Firestore state
summary: Prevent the nightly harvest chain from leaving the live Vault export behind newer Firestore songs when media retries or long-running repair work delay catalog republish.
notes: Opened on 2026-06-14 after the live Vault still showed June 10 as the newest visible song even though Firestore already contained newer June 11 and June 13 records. Investigation proved Cloud Scheduler was still firing daily and recent harvest runs were still republishing latest_catalog_wide.csv, but the published export stayed at 2441 rows while Firestore had already advanced. A manual rebuild_catalog.py run from Firestore on 2026-06-14 republished the export at 2451 rows with newest item 'Fire Does Not Ask Permission' from 2026-06-13T23:20:55.989Z. The first live fix shipped the same day by changing both the Cloud Run harvest entrypoint and the legacy daily_suno_job.sh helper so a zero-row delta manifest no longer exits before metadata enrichment and rebuild_catalog.py. The updated harvest image was rebuilt and redeployed to Cloud Run job generation 20, and a fresh manual execution was started after rollout. A second hardening pass shipped on 2026-06-14 in the viewer/admin layer: `/api/admin/overview` now emits an explicit `exportFreshness` status and the Control Center surfaces healthy/stale/mismatch/unavailable states with automated coverage in `suno-viewer/test/freshness-utils.test.js`. A follow-on pass the same day extended that summary with a `source_ahead` state by comparing newest Firestore song time against newest served export time, so the exact June 14 drift pattern now has a dedicated admin-side signal. A third repair pass was staged later on 2026-06-14 after residual missing-lyrics cards were still visible for older songs like the June 10 Omega Kernel variants: the SUNO repair path had been reading `metadata.prompt` as the primary lyrics source even though archived clip payloads in-repo show a separate top-level `lyrics` field. The local fix now prefers `clip.lyrics`, then `metadata.lyrics`, then `metadata.prompt`, and the Cloud Run entrypoint now also runs `backfill_lyrics_artifacts.py --missing-only` after enrichment so repaired lyric text gets TXT/VTT/JSON artifacts before the next catalog rebuild. On 2026-06-14/15 the viewer also shipped a narrow duplicate-shadow suppression pass and was redeployed live on revision `suno-viewer-00183-f55`, which prevents stale lyricless rows from surfacing when a same-title, same-account, same-day lyric-bearing sibling already exists. Live Firestore verification after that deploy showed the remaining residual lyrics pocket bounded at 64 records. A later June 15 recount improved that again to 47 remaining `lyricsStatus = MISSING` rows, while canonical export freshness advanced to `generatedAt: 2026-06-15T08:51:02Z` with `2456` rows and newest served/source song time `2026-06-14T19:52:17.658Z`. A fresh authenticated manual harvest execution `suno-harvest-jx9ln` was then started on 2026-06-15 to test whether that older residual pocket shrinks further without manual surgery. On 2026-06-16/17 a separate root-cause pass proved the nightly harvest had not actually stopped: Cloud Scheduler `suno-harvest-nightly` stayed enabled, recent Cloud Run executions still completed, and the canonical export was still rebuilding successfully. The real blind spot was the monitor classification. It treated a fresh rebuild of unchanged source data as `healthy`, which meant the product could look stalled for multiple days without tripping the operational alarm if SUNO content creation paused or source freshness stopped advancing materially. Live Firestore verification during that pass showed the latest `sunoSongs.createdAt` was still `2026-06-14T19:52:17.658Z` while `lastSeenAt` was still moving, proving harvest scans were active but source content age had drifted past 57 hours. A permanent hardening patch was then shipped in `yt-ingest/pipeline_monitor.py` and covered by `yt-ingest/validate_pipeline_monitor_status.py`: post-harvest status now separately classifies `source_idle` and `source_scan_stale`, includes source freshness in the written summary and digest, and only suppresses post-harvest email when source content freshness, source scan freshness, catalog freshness, and queue health are all actually green. The updated harvest image was redeployed live to Cloud Run job generation 21. On 2026-06-17 the viewer then shipped the matching customer-facing transparency fix: `freshness-utils.js` now emits `source_idle` when the export matches source but the source content itself is older than threshold, `server.js` exposes that summary through `/api/vault/freshness`, and `VaultGrid.tsx` renders a visible banner on both `sundrop.cloud/vault` and `sundrop.music/vault` explaining that the Vault is synced but the latest source song is old. That viewer pass was validated by automated freshness tests, production build, and live browser verification after deploy on revision `suno-viewer-00192-bm8`. On 2026-06-17 a follow-up proof using the live public Suno profile API showed this was no longer just an upstream drought: `https://studio-api.prod.suno.com/api/profiles/unshakableechos2341` was already returning newer June 15 clips such as `Fire Does Not Ask Permission` (`2026-06-15T04:42:36.632Z`) and `RAMPAGE KILL BILL STYLE` (`2026-06-15T04:26:28.455Z`), while the Vault/Firestore/export still stopped at June 14. That narrowed the failure path to source selection rather than clip-detail fetch. In response, `yt-ingest/catalog_sync_firestore_multi.py` was hardened so the paid/beta fallback floor now always includes `unshakableechos2341`, `genxdreams`, and `gravitystruth`, and any live Firestore registry result is merged with that floor instead of silently replacing it. The script now also records `registry_warning` and `fallback_injected` in `delta_report.json`, and a focused regression test (`yt-ingest/test_catalog_sync_sources.py`) covers the merge behavior. On 2026-06-18 the next production proof established the deeper GenX incident shape: public Suno for `genxdreams` was already ahead into May, while the published catalog still had GenX frozen at April 7; direct Firestore `sources` inspection showed the live registry was missing `genxdreams` entirely; and although a hardened harvest image had been built on June 18, the Cloud Run job itself had not yet been updated and was still running the older spec. The job was manually updated to generation 22 and a patched manual execution `suno-harvest-cmldj` was started on image digest `sha256:51006371339b66196c97d9af8923c1d13f122bb86309b2ccf09b493046d71afd`. Live execution logs from that run already prove the repaired lane is active: `genxdreams: 32 delta rows (new=19, missing_gcs=9, metadata_repairs=4)`, multiple GenX media objects are being written under `gs://aeonimus-suno-media/suno/handles/genxdreams/`, and direct Firestore spot-check confirms missing May songs such as `Sold for Roses` (`f7ea9223-02d8-4b6b-a2e0-24f2d05b2bf6`, `2026-05-07T16:36:19.107Z`) are now landing again. Remaining work is to let that execution finish and then verify the canonical export and visible Vault advance for GenX as well as Vanessa.
